title: Count once on ingest, read tiny rows forever after
caption: The stream job folds clicks into (ad, minute) counters; the dashboard never touches raw events.

steps.text: Every click is appended to a partitioned stream, keyed by ad_id so one ad's events land on one partition.
The stream job keeps a counter per (ad_id, minute) in keyed state and flushes finished buckets as +n upserts, not one write per click.
The raw events are archived too: you'll need them to backfill a new dimension or to fix a bad count.
The dashboard's "last hour for ad1" is 60 point lookups on (ad1, minute), a few kilobytes.

scenarios.name: Job crashes, replays
scenarios.summary: The job flushes its counts, then crashes before its checkpoint: on restart it re-reads from the last checkpoint and adds the same clicks again unless the write is idempotent.

steps.text: The job folds ad1's 12:00 clicks into +120 and upserts it.
It crashes before saving the checkpoint that records how far into the stream it has read.
On restart it rewinds to the last checkpoint and reads those clicks a second time.
A blind +n upsert adds them again: ad1's 12:00 bucket is now too high.
Fix: write the bucket's total (SET count = 120 for (ad1, 12:00)) instead of +n, or commit the writes together with the checkpoint (a transactional sink). A replay then rewrites the same value.

scenarios.name: Alternative: batch rollup
scenarios.summary: A batch job counts the raw log every 5 minutes: no stream state or watermarks to operate, and a rerun simply overwrites buckets, but the numbers are up to 5 minutes old.

steps.text: Clicks are only archived on ingest; nothing counts them yet.
Every 5 minutes a batch job reads the newest files and computes the (ad, minute) counts with a plain GROUP BY.
It overwrites those buckets, so a rerun after a failure is harmless.
The dashboard read is the same 60 rows; the newest minutes just show up later.

scenarios.name: Risk: cardinality explosion
scenarios.summary: Adding country and device to the key multiplies the buckets until most hold one click: job state and the rollup table grow toward the size of the raw stream. Aggregate only on what panels filter by.

steps.text: Product asks for clicks per ad × country × device × minute.
The job's keyed state now holds millions of mostly-1 counters; checkpoints balloon and the job falls behind the stream.
The rollup table gets about one row per click, and the cheap 60-row read becomes thousands of rows per ad.
Mitigation: keep the dimensions dashboards really filter by, keep top-N values plus an 'other' bucket, and answer rare breakdowns from the raw log with an OLAP scan.
